record.title: The main biochemical abnormalities of the acute form of uncomplicated and complicated babesiosis in dogs
record.journal: Науковий вісник Львівського національного університету ветеринарної медицини та біотехнологій імені С.З. Ґжицького
record.abstract: Biochemical disorders observed in canine babesiosis are associated with the severity of the disease. The aim of the research is to analyze the biochemical changes in the blood serum of dogs infected with Babesia spp. in the acute form of uncomplicated and complicated babesiosis and to statistically calculate the identified parameters. Blood serum samples with the following biochemical analysis were collected from 55 dogs that were naturally infected with babesia and were admitted for treatment to the State University Clinic VetCenter of the Training and Production Center for Clinical Veterinary Medicine of the Stepan Gzhytskyi National University of Veterinary Medicine and Biotechnology of Lviv and three private veterinary clinics in Lviv in the period from September 2023 to May 2025. The main biochemical disorders identified in the infected animals include hyperbilirubinemia (63.64 % of dogs), among which clinical symptoms suggesting jaundice were observed only in 17.14 % of animals; increased activity of transaminases – ALT (25.45 %), AST (83.64 %), alkaline phosphatase (80.0 %); azotemia (increase in blood urea nitrogen 47.27 %, creatinine 20.0 %); hypoglycemia and hyperglycemia (9.09 % and 30.91 %, respectively) with no clinical symptoms of hypoglycemia; and alterations in serum electrolyte profile, specifically hypokalemia (40.0 %), hyponatremia (24.0 %), hypo- and hyperchloremia (4.0 % and 20.0 %, respectively), hypo- and hypercalcemia (28.0 % and 12.0 %, respectively, in accordance with ionized calcium, and 28.0 % and 20.0 %, respectively, in accordance with calcium), and hyperphosphatemia (43.64 % of cases). We have not identified any statistically significant changes in the protein content of the blood serum of dogs with babesiosis, but we noted a decrease of the albumin-globulin ratio in 40.0 % of infected animals, which is typical for an infectious disease and also indicates a violation of protein metabolism in the case of diffuse liver damage. We identified a high proportion of animals (83.64 % of animals) with a high urea/creatinine ratio, indicating a prerenal etiology of acute renal dysfunction, the most likely caused by hypovolemia, which creates favorable prognostic conditions for preventing the development of renal dysfunction and multiple organs failure in case of timely treatment of animal owners for veterinary care and correction of the volemic status of the animal and, if indicated, the administration of vasoactive drugs. Consequently, the identified biochemical features are the result of hepatopathy, acute renal dysfunction, dehydration, and starvation. The prospects for future research include the study of hyperphosphatemia, which may be an early indicator of disease severity and risk of unfavorable effects.

screening.rationale: Serum biochemistry in 55 naturally infected dogs, uncomplicated vs complicated; hepatopathy, prerenal azotemia, electrolytes, hyperphosphataemia as severity marker.
